Complementarity of patches: can a day's work be assembled nearby? (C)

Source: R/fn_network.R
complementarity.Rd

An isolation penalty, scaled by area rather than count so a knot of fragments does not out-rank a real patch. For each patch, walk outward over the network (cheapest travel first) accumulating neighbouring patch acreage until a target_area day's worth is gathered; the travel cost that bundle required is the isolation measure. A dense cluster assembles the target cheaply; a lone fragment must range far (or cannot gather it at all). The score is flipped so well-connected patches are high and isolated ones are penalised — no day-length assumption, just the area target.

Usage

complementarity(
  net,
  patch_nodes,
  areas,
  target_area = 50,
  cap_q = 0.95,
  cores = 1,
  invert = TRUE
)

Arguments

net

the net element from accessibility (its graph holds the patch nodes).

patch_nodes

the patch_nodes from accessibility, aligned to areas.

areas

numeric patch areas (acres), one per patch_nodes in order.

target_area

a day's worth of patch area to assemble, in acres (default 50; loose — the saturation scale, not a hard quota).

cap_q

upper quantile (on \((0, 1]\)) at which the raw assembly cost is clamped before rescaling (default 0.95). The isolation cost has a long right tail — a lone fragment can range far, and unreachable patches are Inf — so a single outlier otherwise stretches the min–max rescale and flattens the gradient among the patches that actually differ. Costs above the cap_q quantile of the finite costs (and every Inf) are set to that quantile: all such patches count as equally, maximally isolated. The cap is applied to assemble_hr itself, so it also carries through when the raw hours are rescaled downstream (e.g. by rank_index in rank_calculate). NULL disables the cap (then Inf falls back to the worst finite cost, as before).

cores

fork workers for the per-patch distance loop (default 1); the loop is the cost, so cores gives a near-linear speed-up (Unix only; falls back to serial on Windows).

invert

if TRUE (default), return the flipped score \(1 - \tilde c\) (well-connected = high), the index form; raw assembly cost is kept in assemble_hr.

Value

a data.frame with patch_node, assemble_hr (travel hours to gather target_area, clamped at the cap_q quantile; patches that never total it take that capped worst value) and C on \([0, 1]\), in patch_nodes order.

Details

Run on the augmented graph returned by accessibility (patches are already nodes there). Distances are computed one source at a time, so memory stays O(n) for large patch sets.
